sections.what_happened: After the TSE called the runoff for Lula (51.76% to 48.24% at 99.86% counted per 0500-01; AP/TSE final reporting 51.8% to 48.2%, margin nearly 4.4 million votes; term starts January 5, 2027), regional leaders congratulated him: Mexico's Claudia Sheinbaum ('Long live democracy, the people of Brazil won'), Paraguay's Santiago Pena, Uruguay's Yamandu Orsi (said he spoke with Lula), Bolivia's Rodrigo Paz, Cuba's Miguel Diaz-Canel. Lula is the first Brazilian president elected four times and the first since 1989 to win a runoff after finishing second in round one. Voting had been extended two hours after transport delays and bad weather, with both campaigns alleging fairness problems.
sections.what_verified: Reuters reactions roundup + AP count reporting (via Indian Express/Jamaica Observer) + TSE figures agree on winner, margin band (51.76-51.8%) and fourth-term historicity.
sections.what_disputed: Contested aftermath (NOT confirmed as a filed challenge -- see 0600-07): an AP news-summary headline says Flavio Bolsonaro 'calls for' the results to be annulled, but no quote, filing or second report was retrieved; SCMP says only that either campaign COULD cite the two-hour extension to seek annulment. The pre-runoff candidacy-annulment petitions (Oct 21, both campaigns) are a different, earlier matter. No concession or challenge statement from Flavio Bolsonaro himself was retrieved in-window.
sections.why_matters: The region has already picked its reading of Lula's win -- democracy vindicated vs a result to be challenged. Lead with the leaders' congratulations, hold the annulment question as unresolved (see 0600-07), do not present it as filed.
sections.context: Background: FOLLOW-UP to totw-20261026-0500-01 (Brazil result) -- global leaders react to Lula's reelection; final count consolidates at 51.76-51.8%

totw_analysis: Our read: The region has already picked its reading of Lula's win -- democracy vindicated vs a result to be challenged. Lead with the leaders' congratulations, hold the annulment question as unresolved (see 0600-07), do not present it as filed. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Lula's comeback as a brake on Latin America's rightward wave vs Bolsonaro's camp's fairness complaints about the extended voting hours -- does the 4.4-million margin settle it?
